highlights.title: Google owner Alphabet loses $500bn in market value after profit disappoints Wall Street
highlights.summary: Net profit slid 25% from a year earlier to $26.2bn, well short of expectations, though revenue rose to $127.6bn. Shares in the Google parent Alphabet fell double digits Wednesday evening into Thursday trading, erasing hundreds of billions of dollars in stock market value from the $4tn tech giant.
body: The company had reported lower-than-expected profit and a slowdown in its advertising business while it maintained big spending on AI.
Net profit slid 25% from a year earlier to $26.2bn in the July-to-September period, or $2.12 a share, well short of expectations by analysts surveyed by FactSet.
Alphabet booked an $8.7bn loss on its equity investments, which it attributed to its stake in SpaceX, the Elon Musk-led company where shares have struggled since going public in June.
Revenue, however, rose 25% to an enormous $127.6bn. The figure was slightly below the roughly $128bn analysts had forecast.

Shares in the Google parent Alphabet fell double digits Wednesday evening into Thursday trading, erasing hundreds of billions of dollars in stock market value from the $4tn tech giant.

highlights.title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
highlights.summary: To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft's workforce.
body: It’s also time to name the next Elder Scrolls game, and Xbox’s architect of Forza Motorsport is leaving.

It’s the first time the company has presented such an offer to so many employees, expanding greatly upon the retirement offer that was limited to around 9,000 employees earlier this year. It’s all part of an ongoing effort to avoid reducing investment in AI infrastructure by lowering Microsoft’s operating costs and headcount.

“Our total people costs will go down, our cost per head will go up, and my GPU per researcher will go up,” Nadella said on a podcast almost two years ago, responding to a question about AI’s impact on headcount. That’s a financial way of saying Microsoft will have fewer people, but it will offer higher salaries and more tools and AI power to those who remain.

It also helps explain the continued layoffs we’ve seen at Microsoft over the past couple of years. Microsoft has been performing layoffs regularly over the past decade, but over the past couple of years, the layoffs and executive departures have been significant.

highlights.title: Golden State Valkyries v Atlanta Dream: WNBA finals 2026 Game 6 – live
highlights.summary: Dream host Valkyries in opener of best-of-seven series. Dream say concerns went unheeded for 12.30pm start. Reach out to Ella on Bluesky or by email. Valkyries 5-8 Dream, 6.41, first quarter.
body: “We know if we don’t keep it up, we go home,” Dream guard Allisha Gray says in the half-time interview. “I’m not ready for my season to be over yet.”

Golden State found some momentum at the end of the second quarter, getting a three-pointer from Tiffany Hayes and then a layup from Laeticia Amihere off an Atlanta turnover. Those were the Valkyries’ first points off a turnover of the game. The Dream went the final three minutes of the quarter without scoring, but their 20-point lead is comfortable heading into the second half.

It’s too soon to say we’re certainly headed to a Game 7, but it feels like the Dream are one big run from putting this one away. They have more made three-pointers (eight) than Golden State have made field goals (seven). Rhyne Howard has 11 points and went 3-for-5 from deep. Hayes leads the Valkyries with 11, but as a team they are just 26% from the field.

The Valkyries missed three layups in a span of two minutes, which just about sums up their first half. Meanwhile, this sums up Atlanta’s first half: the Dream are 15-0 (!) this season when Angel Reese hits at least one three-pointer. The record for a half-time lead in the WNBA finals is 22 points.

highlights.title: You All Guessed Elder Scrolls 6’s Name, And Now Here’s The Game’s Setup – Report
highlights.summary: After eight years, Xbox is reportedly preparing to reintroduce The Elder Scrolls VI to the world. And this time, the game will apparently get an official subtitle: Sentinel. According to The Verge, Bethesda could reveal the full name next month in celebration of Skyrim's 15th anniversary.
body: The report states that Hammerfell will serve as the setting for Sentinel. It's a massive region that's southwest of Skyrim and probably best known for being playable in The Elder Scrolls Online. As for the narrative, the RPG "will be the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls," per The Verge. That means discovering "the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts" in Sentinel.

It's unknown how much Bethesda will showcase, if the re-reveal does in fact happen in November. However, the report states that gameplay demonstrations are taking place, following up Xbox CEO Asha Sharma saying she saw the game in August. At that time, Sharma teased The Elder Scrolls VI's subtitle, and fans correctly figured out it's Sentinel --at least reportedly right now. She also noted that the game's "scale and grandeur are incredible."

Earlier this year, Skyrim director Todd Howard expressed that he knows his team at Bethesda needs "to get it right" with The Elder Scrolls VI. The majority of people at Bethesda Game Studios are working on the RPG currently.

highlights.title: Mobile’s Halloween tricks and treats: Clash of Clans, Talking Tom, Monopoly Go, Fortnite and more
highlights.summary: Halloween is almost here and with it comes a reliable range of mobile games tapping into the spooky season. In-game events, cosmetics and more can be found across all kinds of genres, as can a sizeable helping of pumpkins, witches and autumnal scenery.
body: Whether it’s Pokémon Sleep turning towards nightmarish ghosts like Gengar, or a growing cast of horror characters in Fortnite, there’s a good chance one game or other will land a scare.

This year, Epic Games, Zynga, The Pokémon Company, Scopely, Intelligent Systems and even The New York Times are among those dressing up their games for the occasion. Many of them also recently landed among our Top 50 Mobile Game Makers of 2026.

The aptly named Fortnitemares event has brought a month of cursed content to Epic Games’ flagship, tapping into a lineup of characters like Freddy Krueger, Ghost Face and Freddy Fazbear. In fact, characters from the Five Nights at Freddy’s universe are going all-in on the fright factor, with their outfits able to show battle damage.

Other IPs trickling in throughout October have included Hollow Knight, Slender Man, Beetlejuice and Obsession. Meanwhile, gameplay has seen players firing pumpkin rockets, teleporting around and dropping into Reload’s Nitemare Island.

highlights.title: Kalshi and its co-founders face felony charges for violating Utah gambling laws
highlights.summary: The Trump administration is trying to stop Utah from enforcing its gambling ban against Kalshi, making Utah the 10th state sued by the US government agency that regulates prediction markets.
body: Meanwhile, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed criminal charges in a state court against Kalshi and its founders on Wednesday. The attorney general’s office provided us with court filings listing charges against KalshiEX, LLC, Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour, and Kalshi co-founder and COO Luana Lopes Lara.

The company and two co-founders each face 13 felony charges and one misdemeanor for violating gambling laws. The charges are based on sports bets offered on Kalshi between September 13 and September 24. “The state did not issue arrest warrants for Monsour and Lopes Lara. Instead, they have been issued summons to respond to the charges in Third District Court in Salt Lake County,” The Salt Lake Tribune wrote.

The Utah News Dispatch quoted a Kalshi statement vowing to fight the charges. “This is a crazy overreach; Utah is clearly playing politics. We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona,” the statement said, referring to similar charges the company beat in Arizona in May.

body: Some users aren’t exactly thrilled with The New York Times’ recipe-tweaking AI tool.

Some NYT readers have pushed back against the feature, citing concerns in the article’s comment section around the environmental impact of widespread AI adoption and the general impact that AI features may have on the user experience. When one user asked if there will be a way to disable the AI feature, Ko responded with, “No, not at this time,” and noted that the feature is “completely optional to use.”

body: The Italian's Mercedes team said that Antonelli had a "viral illness" and had been excused his duties on Thursday by governing body the FIA "as a precaution to give him the chance to rest ahead of the weekend".

Antonelli will seal the championship, and become the youngest winner in Formula 1 history, as long as he does not lose more than two points to team-mate George Russell and one point to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in the grand prix on Sunday.
The only way he could be stopped from tying up the title is if one of Russell and Hamilton wins. Ninth would be enough for Antonelli to become champion if it is Russell, and 10th if it is Hamilton.

highlights.title: BioWare Co-Founder Breaks Down the Problem With AI in Game Development Perfectly
highlights.summary: When Electronic Arts decided to shutter legendary RPG studio BioWare on Oct. 21, Greg Zeschuk, one of BioWare's co-founders alongside Ray Muzyka and Augustine Yip, found out through a flurry of text messages.
body: "I didn't have the immediate impact,” Zeschuk told 80 Level, speaking from his home in Edmonton — the home of BioWare. "I wasn't there to share in the moment, which in some ways was nice because I was able to kind of just take my time with it."

Zeschuk clarified that this didn't mean the closure wasn't sad or monumental, adding that Edmonton would be hit the hardest by the studio's shutdown. However, Zeschuk said he and his fellow co-founder, Muzyka, had already said their emotional goodbye when they left the studio in 2012. His empathy, however, is more reserved for those who have lost their jobs.
"Anyone getting put into the job hunt is a sort of terrifying endeavor and super sad,” Zeschuk said.

While Zeschuk's feelings about BioWare's closure weren't overtly emotional, he had plenty of passion and ire to direct at executives with no game development experience, and at their over-involvement and reliance on AI.

highlights.title: Data centers could send US climate pollution skyrocketing
highlights.summary: The US power sector could release 42 percent more planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution by 2030 than it did in 2025 as it builds out more fossil fuel infrastructure to meet data center electricity demand, according to a new analysis by the Sierra Club.
body: Gas plants built for data centers are poised to undo more than a decade of climate action.

CO2 emissions from electricity generation would increase by 618 million tons by the end of the decade if planned AI projects are constructed. That’s roughly equivalent to carbon pollution from the electricity use of 128,788,523 homes in a year.

The Sierra Club’s estimate is higher than some previous projections from other groups. Another study published by academic researchers in June forecast that electricity demand from data centers and crypto mines could push up power sector emissions by 28 percent by 2030 when compared to a scenario with no data center growth. The outcome depends on how many planned data center projects actually come to fruition, as well as on what type of technology is used to power those facilities.

highlights.title: Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race
highlights.summary: The French AI lab claims its latest release matches or outperforms even the best models from DeepSeek and Z.ai in coding and cybersecurity.
body: A few weeks ago, French company Mistral released an early version of its new artificial intelligence model, nicknamed Le Chonk. At the time, the company said it was the most advanced open-weight offering outside of China. After further refinement, Mistral now says Le Chonk is the “world’s best” open-weight model for automated coding and cybersecurity.

The advances, Mistral says, were made possible by feeding the model increasingly difficult cybersecurity and coding problems, which allowed the trillion-parameter Le Chonk to match or surpass models from leading Chinese labs like DeepSeek and Z.ai.

“It’s a pivotal moment in the global AI leadership race,” Pierre Stock, VP of science at Mistral, told reporters during a press briefing. “It offers frontier capabilities for enterprises and governments to defend against an increasing threat level in cyber.”

The finalized version of Le Chonk is now freely available for anybody to access. After a flurry of AI-related cybersecurity incidents, Mistral claims that it’s important for the West to have its own advanced open-weight models. “You have no guarantee that [Chinese models] won’t behave maliciously. They can be threat vectors,” Stock said.

highlights.title: 28 Years Later, Ocarina of Time’s Saddest Line Is Still the Best in Zelda History
highlights.summary: Few things can elicit a good cry like a sad video game. And Roger… ’s gut-punch portrayal of living with dementia. Spiritfarer ’s calming meditation on life, death, and the passage between.
body: Maybe a good cry isn’t always the reason we play games, but it springs upon us nevertheless. And one of the strongest instances actually dates back two decades, to Nintendo’s totemic 3D adventure game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Early in the adventure, after proving he has what it takes to be a hero and receiving the blessing of the dying Great Deku Tree, young Link finally prepares to say goodbye to Kokiri Forest. Before he can venture past its edge, his childhood friend catches up to him. Saria is sad to see him go, but she has a parting gift for him: the ocarina from which the game gets its name.
“I knew… that you would leave the forest… someday, Link,” she says. “Because you’re different from me and my friends… But that’s OK, because we’ll be friends forever…won’t we?”

highlights.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
highlights.summary: Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company's stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history.
body: The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story’s publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day.

While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google’s Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That’s about a billion more than analyst guesses.

Google is still making a huge amount of money, but there are several troubling trends emerging. The last few years at the company have been all about AI, with generative technology appearing in products from Gmail to Android. Most notably, Google is shifting to an AI search platform powered by Gemini models.

highlights.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
highlights.summary: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma. By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been.
body: And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings.
Yet, apparently, a crisis of a sort has been churning just below the surface of what is, by broad consensus, Europe’s best home support.

On Friday, Dortmund had announced a kind of bribery scheme. A rewards program is probably a kinder way of putting it. Fans who stayed off their phones during the bout with Eintracht had the chance to win signed jerseys and earn gift cards to the club’s merchandise store. If they activated a so-called “fan mode” on the club’s app – a name so phenomenally passive-aggressive you can only applaud whoever came up with it – the club could count who unlocked their phones the fewest times during the game. For every minute the fans left their phones alone, they got points.
Dortmund are not the only German team to pick a fight with phones.

body: With this in mind, we asked music fans why they favour discs over other formats, and if it is a new preference or a lifetime habit.

Andrew Wales, 67, from London, owns “well over 10,000” CDs. “My wife’s very considerate,” he says over the phone. “There’s quite a few in this room where I’m speaking.” They have also spilt into the next bedroom and into the corridor.

“I don’t need Spotify,” says Wales. “The fact is, I like listening to music and I have always preferred owning it in a physical form. The [size of the] CD format allows me to own the number I own despite living in a two-bedroom flat and not a country mansion, so that’s another bonus.”

Much of the classical music Wales buys and listens to is available only on CD. “I bought my first CD in 1991 – John Scofield, Meant to Be – around the same time that I bought my first CD player. LPs were becoming increasingly shoddy, both in terms of pressing and presentation, and their limitations meant that often or not songs or tracks were included on the CD release, but not on LP. There are still cases where that happens today.”

highlights.title: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
highlights.summary: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded.
body: AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. That’s why EU regulators and US agencies are rightfully calling for agent developers and deployers to monitor agents in real time. But these rules assume that companies can see what their agents are doing and why—when in reality, they lack sufficient visibility.

As agents roll out across critical sectors, from finance to government to medicine, we must be able to monitor them in real time to prevent wide-ranging and potentially devastating consequences. And while safety depends on monitoring, monitoring requires observability: the capacity to capture what the system did, process it into signals, and present those to humans or automated oversight systems. In other words, we need to know what the agent did and why it did it. And as our recent research shows, current agent frameworks—the software that runs agents— do not reliably generate the crucial observability records we need to ensure that agents are deployed safely.

highlights.title: How the Best Peptide Skin-Care Can Deliver Botox-Like Results
highlights.summary: Peptides skincare—a.k.a. the “silent powerhouse”—can do everything from stimulate collagen and elastin production to slow down to cellular processes.
body: Given all the peptides buzz, you might be wondering what the best peptide skin-care products can do for you, and if they really are the gold standard of anti-aging skincare. These “silent powerhouses” (there are, in fact, various types of peptides) are a derm favorite for healing skin, slowing aging, and stimulating collagen, reducing puffiness, and boosting skin elasticity. At their most basic, peptides are short chains of amino acids that form the building blocks of proteins like collagen, elastin, and keratin. These proteins are essential for firm, youthful-looking skin.

According to board-certified dermatologist Brendan Camp, MD, peptides are garnering a lot of attention right now because they offer a range of skin benefits without being harsh or irritating. Unlike some ingredients that have had their moment in the spotlight and since faded from focus, peptides for skin tend to be well-tolerated and easy to incorporate into a daily routine, which is why they are likely here to stay. He also notes that peptides can be especially helpful during post-procedure recovery, since they support the skin barrier and aid overall healing.
points: Peptides skincare—a.k.a. the “silent powerhouse”—can do everything from stimulate collagen and elastin production to slow down to cellular processes.
